 NZ vs IND, 1st T20I preview: Sleep-deprived India face chilly Christchurch test
 NZ vs IND, 1st T20I preview, and team news: India arrive in Christchurch short on sleep and preparation time after a hectic run of T20Is. Shreyas Iyer's men must quickly adapt to chilly, windy conditions against a New Zealand side.
 Advertisement Can Gambhir and Iyer lead India to win in New Zealand? (PTI Photo) By: Akshay Ramesh New Delhi , Oct 22, 2026 02:35 IST Last Updated Oct 22, 2026 02:35 IST Published by Akshay Ramesh Oct 22, 2026 02:35 IST India have barely had time to catch their breath. After wrapping up a five-match T20I series against the West Indies on October 18, they flew to New Zealand two days later and squeezed in two training sessions before the series opener in Christchurch, scheduled for Thursday, October 22.
 “We are getting less sleep. But, for us, the more matches we play, the better it is,” Shreyas Iyer said on the eve of the first T20I. The schedule tells its own story. India have played 21 T20Is since the IPL 2026 season ended, more than any other team, with Sri Lanka the next busiest among Test-playing nations with 11. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story WHEN AND WHERE TO WATCH?
 India will take on New Zealand in the series opener at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. The match will get underway at 12.30 pm IST (8 pm local time). Sony Sports Network will provide television coverage in India, while the match will be streamed live on SonyLIV.
 For Iyer, the demands of the calendar have been relentless. The new captain has endured mixed results, losing to Ireland and England away from home before winning against Afghanistan in India. The team then travelled to Japan to defend its Asian Games gold medal before returning home for the five-match T20I series against the West Indies.
 The travel itinerary makes for exhausting reading. After the IPL, India flew to Ireland for two T20Is in June. They travelled to England for five matches in July before taking on a packed schedule over the last two months. India have played 11 T20Is in that period, with some players also juggling commitments across formats.
 “We have been playing so continuously, from Japan to India, from India to New Zealand," Iyer said.
 "Continuously, we are used to it now, in a way. So, this pattern has been set in our system. We are getting less sleep, but the more matches we play, the better it is for us,” he added.
 Iyer was candid about the demands of an unforgiving cricket calendar. Yet, despite the fatigue and the lack of preparation time, the skipper insisted that India would remain focused on winning the series. TESTING CONDITIONS?
 That might be easier said than done. India have already paid the price for a lack of time to acclimatise to unfamiliar conditions, losing 0-2 to Ireland in a historic first before ending their England T20I tour without a win. They have since dominated Afghanistan and the West Indies at home, but New Zealand presents a different challenge, particularly during its early summer.
 Mitchell Santner offered a glimpse of what awaits India in Christchurch. Speaking to the press on the eve of the match, the New Zealand captain warned that the conditions could be cold and windy on Thursday.
 “The cold. If it’s foreign conditions that you are not used to in terms of bounce and nip, it’s going to be hard to acclimatise. When we were in India, it was hot and humid and it took us some time to get used to it. Temperature wise, it takes a bit of time to get used to it. It might be windy, cold tomorrow night. But, once you are in the heat of the battle, I think you can get into it,” he said.
 advertisement The late start, at 8 pm local time, could make matters more complicated. Wind and cold will test the players, while the possibility of dew could influence how the match unfolds. The team bowling second may have to contend with a slippery ball, making the toss a potentially crucial factor.
 India will also have to make a significant adjustment with the bat. Their recent home series against the West Indies was played on flat surfaces, where 200-plus totals became the norm. New Zealand is unlikely to offer the same conditions. It has been 16 innings since a 200-plus total was recorded in a T20I in the country.
 India will need to recalibrate their approach, and quickly. The challenge is not just about adapting to the conditions but also about doing so with limited time to recover from a demanding schedule. After weeks of travel and almost uninterrupted cricket, the visitors have little room to ease themselves into the series. advertisement INDIA vs NEW ZEALAND H2H
 India have won 19 and lost 11 of their 31 T20Is against New Zealand.
 Their recent record on New Zealand soil offers some encouragement. India won the five-match series 5-0 in 2020 before taking a three-match series 1-0 in 2022.
 The two teams last met in the 2026 T20 World Cup final, where India smashed 255 before bowling the Black Caps out for 159 in Ahmedabad. INDIA vs NEW ZEALAND TEAM NEWS
 Bhuvneshwar Kumar (right) is expected to start for India in Christchurch on Thursday (PTI Photo) 
 All eyes will be on Bhuvneshwar Kumar, who returns to the T20I fold. The experienced seamer made his comeback after nearly four years in the fifth T20I against the West Indies in Bengaluru last week. However, the s eries-deciding match was washed out due to rain, leaving India with little opportunity to assess him in a full contest.
 advertisement Bhuvneshwar will be hoping to make the most of the nip on offer in New Zealand's early summer. His experience could prove invaluable to an Indian pace attack that will be without Jasprit Bumrah and all-rounder Hardik Pandya.
 India will also welcome Varun Chakravarthy back into the side. The spinner returns for the first time since suffering an injury during the home series against Afghanistan last month.
 Then there is the familiar Vaibhav Sooryavanshi question: will he play or will he have to wait a little longer? The 15-year-old opener made his T20I debut in England and featured at the Asian Games, but has since spent time on the sidelines. He was not given an opportunity during the five-match T20I series against the West Indies either.
 Iyer made India's plans clear on Wednesday, indicating that the youngster would have to wait for his chances. India are set to begin the series with the tried-and-tested opening combination of Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma.
 There is another selection question for the team management to address. Naman Dhir showed his potential with the bat against the West Indies and also chipped in with useful overs of off-spin. India must decide whether to retain him or opt for a different combination.
 advertisement Given the conditions in New Zealand, India could turn to two medium-pace-bowling all-rounders in Shivam Dube and Nitish Kumar Reddy. That would allow them to strengthen their seam-bowling options while accommodating Varun in the XI.
 New Zealand, meanwhile, have their own injury concerns. Explosive opener Mark Chapman is unavailable, along with all-rounder Rachin Ravindra. Fast bowler Zak Foulkes will also miss the series. However, Santner's side have enough depth to call upon replacements and remain competitive.
 NZ SQUAD: Mitchell Santner (capt), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Josh Clarkson, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Lockie Ferguson, Matt Henry, Bevon Jacobs, Kyle Jamieson, Adam Milne, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Tim Seifert, Nathan Smith, Blair Tickner.
 IND SQUAD: Shreyas Iyer (capt), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan (wk), Tilak Varma (vc), Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav.
 NZ vs IND, 1st T20I PREDICTED XI 
 New Zealand: Finn Allen, Tim Seifert (wk), Devon Conway, Glenn Phillips, Daryl Mitchell, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (capt), Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Lockie Ferguson.
 India: Sanju Samson (wk), Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer (capt), Tilak Varma, Shivam Dube/Naman Dhir, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Varun Chakravarthy, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh. HAGLEY OVAL, CHRISTCHURCH: PITCH AND CONDITIONS
 Christchurch is expected to be cold and windy on Thursday evening, with temperatures hovering around 15 degrees Celsius. There is no threat of rain, so the weather is unlikely to interrupt play, although the conditions could test the players.
 Hagley Oval last hosted a T20I in March this year. South Africa posted 187 after batting first and successfully defended the total, winning by 33 runs.
 The boundaries at Hagley Oval are bigger than those at several other venues, while the conditions are expected to offer movement for fast bowlers. With the ball likely to do more than it did during India's recent home series, a high-scoring contest might not be on the cards. India will have to adapt quickly if they are to begin the tour on a winning note. - Ends
